messages.content:
Source (study summary): 'In a trial of 214 adults, participants who took a 20-minute nap scored 11% higher on an afternoon memory test than a no-nap control group. No benefit was observed for naps of 60 minutes.'

Claim to check: 'Napping improves memory by 11%.'

Verdict: distorted. The number is real, but the claim strips out every condition that makes it true.
- 'improves memory by 11%' - the source supports this only for one setup: 'participants who took a 20-minute nap scored 11% higher on an afternoon memory test'. The claim widens it to napping and memory in general.
- The source explicitly limits the effect: 'No benefit was observed for naps of 60 minutes.' The claim omits this, implying any nap helps.
- The 11% is a score gap against 'a no-nap control group' in a single trial of 214 adults, not a universal improvement figure.
Accurate version: 'In one trial, a 20-minute nap was followed by scores 11% higher on an afternoon memory test; 60-minute naps showed no benefit.'

Source (spec sheet): Model K-9 blender. Capacity: 1.8 L. Motor: 900 W. Weight: 3.2 kg. Warranty: 2 years, parts only.

Claim to check: 'The K-9 has a 1.8-litre capacity, a 900-watt motor, weighs 3.2 kg, and comes with a two-year parts warranty.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "capacity 1.8 L", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "Capacity: 1.8 L"}, {"element": "motor 900 W", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "Motor: 900 W"}, {"element": "weight 3.2 kg", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "Weight: 3.2 kg"}, {"element": "two-year parts warranty", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "Warranty: 2 years, parts only"}], "overall": "supported"}

Source (forecast bulletin): 'Rain is likely this evening, with a 70% chance of showers after 6 pm. Temperatures will fall to around 8 C overnight. Gusts of up to 40 km/h are expected near the coast.'

Claim to check: 'It will rain this evening, temperatures will drop to 8 degrees, and there will be 40 km/h gusts.'

Verdict: mostly supported, with one hedge dropped and one scope slip.
- 'It will rain this evening' - distorted. The source says rain is 'likely', with 'a 70% chance of showers after 6 pm'. A 70% likelihood is not a certainty; the claim upgrades it to one.
- 'temperatures will drop to 8 degrees' - supported in substance: temperatures 'will fall to around 8 C overnight'. The source's 'around' makes the figure approximate; the claim's flat '8' is a minor tightening.
- '40 km/h gusts' - supported as a maximum ('gusts of up to 40 km/h'), but the source limits them to 'near the coast', and the claim drops that location limit.

Source (results statement): 'Revenue for the year rose 6% to $48.2 million. Operating profit was $5.6 million, down from $6.1 million.'

Claim to check: 'Revenue rose 6% to $42.8 million, while operating profit fell to $5.6 million.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "revenue rose 6%", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "Revenue for the year rose 6%"}, {"element": "revenue reached $42.8 million", "verdict": "contradicted", "evidence": "rose 6% to $48.2 million - the claim transposes the digits"}, {"element": "operating profit fell to $5.6 million", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "Operating profit was $5.6 million, down from $6.1 million"}], "overall": "distorted"}

Source (transit notice): 'From March 3, the 42 bus will not stop at Elm Street or Pine Street on weekdays, due to roadworks. Weekend service is unchanged.'

Claim to check: 'The 42 bus no longer stops at Elm Street or Pine Street.'

Verdict: distorted - the scope is widened twice.
- The source restricts the change to weekdays: 'will not stop at Elm Street or Pine Street on weekdays'. The claim states it without qualification, as if it applied every day.
- The source says 'Weekend service is unchanged', so on Saturdays and Sundays the bus still stops at both streets - the claim, read plainly, contradicts that.
- The change also only begins 'From March 3'; the claim's 'no longer' implies it is already in effect at all times.
Accurate version: 'From March 3, the 42 will skip Elm Street and Pine Street on weekdays; weekend stops are unchanged.'

Source (nutrition label): 'Per serving (40 g): sugar 9 g, fibre 2 g. Pack size: 200 g (5 servings).'

Claim to check: 'The whole pack contains just 9 g of sugar.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "whole pack contains 9 g of sugar", "verdict": "contradicted", "evidence": "Per serving (40 g): sugar 9 g; Pack size: 200 g (5 servings) - 9 g is per serving, so the whole pack contains 5 x 9 g = 45 g"}], "overall": "contradicted"}

Source (plaque on the building): 'This mill was built in 1873 by the Hartley brothers. At its peak in 1890 it employed 60 workers.'

Claim to check: 'The Hartley brothers built this mill in 1873, and at its peak in 1890 it employed 60 workers.'

Verdict: supported. Every element of the claim is in the source, with no condition dropped or widened.
- Builders and date: 'built in 1873 by the Hartley brothers' - matches exactly.
- Employment figure: 'At its peak in 1890 it employed 60 workers' - the claim keeps both the 'peak' qualifier and the year, so the 60 is not presented as a typical workforce.
Nothing in the claim goes beyond the plaque.

Source (guidance leaflet): 'Adults with mild symptoms may take up to 3 g per day. This guidance does not apply to children under 12, for whom no dose has been established.'

Claim to check: 'It is safe for the whole family at up to 3 grams a day.'

Verdict: distorted, and partly contradicted.
- 'the whole family' - contradicted. The source states plainly: 'This guidance does not apply to children under 12'. Children are excluded, not included.
- 'safe' - unsupported as stated. The source says adults 'may take up to 3 g per day'; it gives a permitted dose for a defined group ('Adults with mild symptoms'), not a blanket safety guarantee for everyone.
- The 3 g figure itself is supported, but only for adults with mild symptoms.
Accurate version: 'Adults with mild symptoms may take up to 3 g per day; the guidance does not cover children under 12.'

Source (match report): 'Okafor scored twice in the second half, and the match ended 2-1 to the home side.'

Claim to check: 'Okafor scored a hat-trick as the home side won 2-1.'

Verdict: partly contradicted.
- 'scored a hat-trick' - contradicted. The source says Okafor 'scored twice'; a hat-trick is three goals.
- 'the home side won 2-1' - supported: 'the match ended 2-1 to the home side'.
Accurate version: 'Okafor scored twice in the second half as the home side won 2-1.'

Source (staff memo): 'From January, staff with at least one year of service may work remotely for up to two days per week, subject to their manager's approval.'

Draft announcement to check: 'Great news: everyone can now work from home two days a week.'

Verdict: distorted. The headline number survives, but both conditions in the memo are dropped.
- 'everyone' - the memo restricts eligibility to 'staff with at least one year of service'. Newer staff are not covered.
- Approval: the memo makes remote days 'subject to their manager's approval'. The draft presents it as an automatic entitlement.
- 'two days a week' - supported as a maximum: the memo says 'up to two days per week'. It is a cap, not a guaranteed allocation.
Accurate version: 'From January, staff with a year or more of service can apply to work remotely up to two days a week, with their manager's approval.'

Source (study report): 'In a survey of 900 nurses, researchers found a correlation between higher coffee intake and lower self-reported stress. The study did not test whether coffee caused the difference.'

Headline to check: 'Coffee reduces stress, a study of healthcare workers has found.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "coffee reduces stress", "verdict": "distorted", "evidence": "found a correlation between higher coffee intake and lower self-reported stress; The study did not test whether coffee caused the difference - a correlation is upgraded to a cause"}, {"element": "study of healthcare workers", "verdict": "distorted", "evidence": "In a survey of 900 nurses - the sample was nurses only, not healthcare workers generally"}], "overall": "distorted"}

Source (warranty terms): 'This warranty covers defects in materials and workmanship for three years from the date of purchase. It does not cover accidental damage, water damage, or use in a commercial setting.'

Claim to check: 'It is covered for three years, whatever happens.'

Verdict: contradicted.
- The three-year period is supported: 'covers defects in materials and workmanship for three years from the date of purchase'.
- 'Whatever happens' is directly contradicted by the exclusions: 'It does not cover accidental damage, water damage, or use in a commercial setting.' Coverage is limited to defects, not all events.
Accurate version: 'Defects in materials and workmanship are covered for three years; accidental and water damage and commercial use are excluded.'

Source (official results): 'Turnout by district: North 61%, South 58%, East 64%, West 59%.'

Claim to check: 'East recorded the highest turnout of the four districts, at 64%.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "East turnout was 64%", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "East 64%"}, {"element": "East had the highest turnout", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "North 61%, South 58%, East 64%, West 59% - 64% is the largest of the four figures"}], "overall": "supported"}

Source (user manual): 'Charge the battery for at least 4 hours before first use. Do not expose the device to temperatures above 45 C.'

FAQ draft to check: 'A quick one-hour charge is all you need before using the device for the first time.'

Verdict: contradicted. The manual requires 'at least 4 hours' of charging before first use; the draft's 'one-hour charge' is a quarter of the specified minimum. A user following the FAQ would undercharge the battery against the manufacturer's instruction.

Source (museum label): 'This bowl, dated to around 1200 BCE, was excavated at Tell Amra in 1932. Similar bowls from the site were used to store grain.'

Claim to check: 'This bowl, made around 1200 BCE, was used to store grain.'

Verdict: distorted - one fact is transferred from other objects to this one.
- 'made around 1200 BCE' - supported: the bowl is 'dated to around 1200 BCE'.
- 'was used to store grain' - distorted. The label attributes grain storage to 'Similar bowls from the site', not to this bowl. The claim moves a property of comparable objects onto this specific artifact, which the source does not state.
Accurate version: 'This bowl, from around 1200 BCE, is of a type that was used to store grain.'

Source (results statement): 'Profit fell 12% to $3.1 million, mainly due to a one-off restructuring charge of $0.9 million.'

Claim to check: 'Profits fell 12% because restructuring was the company's main cost this year, at $0.9 million.'

Verdict: partly distorted.
- 'Profits fell 12%' - supported: 'Profit fell 12% to $3.1 million'.
- 'a one-off restructuring charge of $0.9 million' as the main reason for the fall - supported: the fall was 'mainly due to' that charge.
- 'the company's main cost this year' - unsupported. The source says the charge was the main cause of the profit fall, not that it was the company's largest cost. A $0.9 million charge can drive a profit decline without being the biggest item in the cost base; the source gives no ranking of costs.
Accurate version: 'Profits fell 12%, mainly due to a one-off restructuring charge of $0.9 million.'

Source (recipe card): 'Makes 12 muffins. Bake at 180 C for 22-25 minutes.'

Claim to check: 'This recipe makes a dozen muffins, baked at 180 in under 25 minutes.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "makes a dozen muffins", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "Makes 12 muffins"}, {"element": "baked at 180", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "Bake at 180 C"}, {"element": "in under 25 minutes", "verdict": "distorted", "evidence": "for 22-25 minutes - the range tops out at exactly 25 minutes, so 'under 25' understates the maximum bake time"}], "overall": "distorted"}

Source (school newsletter): 'During exam week (June 9-13), the library will stay open until 8 pm on Tuesday and Thursday. On other days, normal hours apply and the library closes at 6 pm.'

Claim to check: 'The library is open until 8 every night during exam week.'

Verdict: distorted - the scope is widened.
- The late opening applies on two named days only: 'until 8 pm on Tuesday and Thursday'.
- The source is explicit about the rest of the week: 'On other days, normal hours apply and the library closes at 6 pm.'
So 'every night' is wrong for Monday, Wednesday and Friday of exam week.
Accurate version: 'The library stays open until 8 pm on Tuesday and Thursday of exam week.'

Source (water quality report): 'Lead: 4 ppb (limit 15 ppb). Copper: 0.8 ppm (limit 1.3 ppm). Nitrate: 6 ppm (limit 10 ppm).'

Claim to check: 'All three measured contaminants were within their limits.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "lead within limit", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "Lead: 4 ppb (limit 15 ppb)"}, {"element": "copper within limit", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "Copper: 0.8 ppm (limit 1.3 ppm)"}, {"element": "nitrate within limit", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "Nitrate: 6 ppm (limit 10 ppm)"}], "overall": "supported"}

Source (product announcement): 'The Pro model adds a second cooling fan and ships in November. The standard model is unchanged.'

Claim to check: 'Both models get a second cooling fan when the new range ships in November.'

Verdict: distorted.
- The second fan belongs to one model only: 'The Pro model adds a second cooling fan'.
- The standard model is explicitly excluded: 'The standard model is unchanged.' Extending the fan to 'both models' contradicts that sentence.
- The November timing is supported for the Pro: it 'ships in November'.
Accurate version: 'The Pro model, shipping in November, adds a second cooling fan; the standard model is unchanged.'

Source (survey report): 'Of 1,200 respondents, 54% said they somewhat or strongly support the plan, 31% said they oppose it, and 15% were unsure.'

Claim to check: 'A majority of residents strongly support the plan.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "a majority strongly support", "verdict": "distorted", "evidence": "54% said they somewhat or strongly support the plan - the 54% merges 'somewhat' with 'strongly', so the strongly-only share is not given and cannot be shown to be a majority"}, {"element": "residents", "verdict": "distorted", "evidence": "Of 1,200 respondents - the figures describe the survey sample, and the source does not establish that respondents mirror all residents"}], "overall": "distorted"}

Source (pool notice): 'In winter (December to February), the pool closes at 7 pm on Sundays. Summer hours differ.'

Claim to check, posted in mid-December: 'The pool closes at 7 pm on Sundays at the moment.'

Verdict: supported.
- December falls inside the source's winter window: 'In winter (December to February), the pool closes at 7 pm on Sundays'.
- The claim's 'at the moment' matches that seasonal scope - it does not claim the 7 pm closing applies year-round, which the source would not support ('Summer hours differ').

Source (biography excerpt): 'She published her first novel at 29, after three rejections. It sold 4,000 copies in its first year.'

Claim to check: 'Her debut novel, published when she was 29, was a bestseller that sold 40,000 copies in its first year.'

Verdict: distorted, with one figure contradicted.
- 'published when she was 29' - supported: 'published her first novel at 29'.
- 'sold 40,000 copies' - contradicted: the source says '4,000 copies in its first year'. The claim adds a zero.
- 'a bestseller' - unsupported. The source makes no bestseller claim, and 4,000 first-year copies is not presented as one.
Accurate version: 'Her debut novel, published when she was 29 after three rejections, sold 4,000 copies in its first year.'

Source (spec sheet): 'Weight: 1.29 kg. Battery life: up to 14 hours (video playback, Wi-Fi off).'

Claim to check: 'It weighs 1.29 kg and the battery lasts 14 hours.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "weighs 1.29 kg", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "Weight: 1.29 kg"}, {"element": "battery lasts 14 hours", "verdict": "distorted", "evidence": "Battery life: up to 14 hours (video playback, Wi-Fi off) - 'up to' states a maximum under specific conditions, not a guaranteed duration"}], "overall": "distorted"}

Source (committee minutes): 'The committee agreed to revisit the budget in September. No decision was taken on the venue.'

Claim to check: 'The committee decided to move the venue and will revisit the budget in September.'

Verdict: half supported, half contradicted.
- 'decided to move the venue' - contradicted. The minutes state the opposite: 'No decision was taken on the venue.'
- 'will revisit the budget in September' - supported: 'agreed to revisit the budget in September'.
Accurate version: 'The committee will revisit the budget in September; the venue remains undecided.'

Source (trial report): 'Phase II trial, 86 patients. After 8 weeks, symptom scores had fallen by 18% in the drug group and by 9% in the placebo group. The authors state that larger trials are needed to confirm efficacy.'

Claim to check: 'The drug is proven to cut symptoms by 18%.'

Verdict: distorted in two ways.
- 'cut symptoms by 18%' - the 18% is the fall within the drug group, but the placebo group also fell 9%: 'symptom scores had fallen by 18% in the drug group and by 9% in the placebo group'. The advantage over placebo is 9 points, not 18.
- 'proven' - contradicted by the source's own caution: this is a 'Phase II trial' of 86 patients and 'larger trials are needed to confirm efficacy'. A preliminary result awaiting confirmation is not proof.
Accurate version: 'In a small Phase II trial, symptoms fell 18% on the drug versus 9% on placebo; larger trials are needed.'

Source (rail notice): 'The 07:15 to Carlisle is cancelled on Saturday only, due to engineering works. A replacement bus departs at 07:20. Sunday services run as normal.'

Claim to check: 'There is no 07:15 train this weekend - take the 07:20 bus instead.'

Verdict: distorted.
- The cancellation is for one day: 'cancelled on Saturday only'. The claim's 'this weekend' sweeps Sunday in as well.
- Sunday is explicitly normal: 'Sunday services run as normal', so the 07:15 runs on Sunday and no bus is needed.
- The 07:20 replacement bus is supported, but only as the Saturday alternative.
Accurate version: 'The 07:15 is cancelled on Saturday (bus at 07:20); on Sunday it runs as normal.'

Source (fund announcement): 'The fund awards up to $50,000 per project. Only registered charities may apply. Application deadline: May 1.'

Claim to check: 'Any community group can receive $50,000 if they apply by May 1.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "any community group can receive", "verdict": "contradicted", "evidence": "Only registered charities may apply"}, {"element": "receive $50,000", "verdict": "distorted", "evidence": "awards up to $50,000 per project - $50,000 is a ceiling, not an entitlement"}, {"element": "apply by May 1", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "Application deadline: May 1"}], "overall": "distorted"}

Source (news report): 'The skeleton was radiocarbon dated to between 3,200 and 3,400 years ago. A bronze pin was found beside it. Researchers believe the individual may have been a metalworker, though this is uncertain.'

Claim to check: 'Archaeologists have found the 3,400-year-old skeleton of a metalworker.'

Verdict: distorted - both the date and the occupation are stated more firmly than the source allows.
- '3,400-year-old' - the source gives a range: 'dated to between 3,200 and 3,400 years ago'. The claim takes the top of the range and presents it as the exact age.
- 'of a metalworker' - the source hedges this twice: researchers 'believe the individual may have been a metalworker, though this is uncertain'. The claim drops the hedge and states it as established fact.
Accurate version: 'Archaeologists have found a skeleton dated to 3,200-3,400 years ago, possibly of a metalworker.'

Source (changelog): 'Version 2.3: fixes a crash when exporting PDFs larger than 100 MB. Startup time on Windows is about 10% faster.'

Claim to check: 'Version 2.3 makes the app 10% faster overall.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "10% faster", "verdict": "distorted", "evidence": "Startup time on Windows is about 10% faster - the 10% applies to startup time on one platform, not to the app's overall speed"}, {"element": "crash fix", "verdict": "unsupported", "evidence": "the claim does not mention the PDF export crash fix, which is the update's other change; nothing in the claim is contradicted on this point"}], "overall": "distorted"}

Source (rental listing): 'Rent: $1,450 per month, utilities not included. Deposit: one month's rent. Pets: none permitted, except fish.'

Claim to check: '$1,450 a month covers everything, and pets are welcome.'

Verdict: contradicted on both points.
- 'covers everything' - the listing states 'utilities not included', and a deposit of one month's rent is also due. The $1,450 is rent only.
- 'pets are welcome' - the listing says 'none permitted, except fish'. Only fish are allowed.
Accurate version: 'Rent is $1,450 a month plus utilities, with a month's deposit; no pets except fish.'

Source (survey report): 'Volunteers counted 312 swifts at the colony this June, up from 289 last June. The organisers note that counts vary with the weather and with the number of volunteers taking part.'

Claim to check: 'The swift population grew by 23 birds this year.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "grew by 23", "verdict": "distorted", "evidence": "counted 312 swifts ... up from 289 - the arithmetic 312 - 289 = 23 is correct for the counts, but a count difference is not a measured population change"}, {"element": "the swift population grew", "verdict": "unsupported", "evidence": "counts vary with the weather and with the number of volunteers taking part - the source itself gives reasons the count can move without the population changing"}], "overall": "distorted"}

Source (recall notice): 'This recall applies to batches B12 to B19, sold between January and March. Other batches are unaffected and remain safe to use.'

Claim to check: 'All units of the product sold this year have been recalled.'

Verdict: contradicted - the scope is far narrower than the claim.
- The recall covers specific batches only: 'batches B12 to B19, sold between January and March'.
- The source explicitly excludes the rest: 'Other batches are unaffected and remain safe to use.' Units sold this year outside those batches and months are not recalled.
Accurate version: 'Batches B12 to B19, sold between January and March, have been recalled; other batches are unaffected.'

Source (statistics release): 'Unemployment fell from 5.2% to 4.9%, a drop of 0.3 percentage points.'

Claim to check: 'Unemployment fell by 0.3% last quarter.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "fell by 0.3%", "verdict": "distorted", "evidence": "a drop of 0.3 percentage points - the fall from 5.2% to 4.9% is 0.3 percentage points; expressed as a percentage change it would be roughly 5.8%, and a 0.3% relative fall would be only about 0.016 points"}], "overall": "distorted"}

Source (event listing): 'Doors 7 pm. Support act on stage 7:45 pm. Headliner on stage 9 pm. Curfew 11 pm.'

Claim to check: 'The headliner starts at 7:45.'
Verdict: contradicted. The listing puts the support act on stage at 7:45 pm: 'Support act on stage 7:45 pm'. The headliner is listed separately and later: 'Headliner on stage 9 pm'.

Source (policy wording): 'The policy pays out if a flight is delayed by more than 4 hours due to weather or a mechanical fault. Delays caused by strikes are excluded.'

Claim to check: 'You are covered for any flight delay over four hours.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "covered for any delay over four hours", "verdict": "distorted", "evidence": "pays out if a flight is delayed by more than 4 hours due to weather or a mechanical fault - cover depends on the cause, not just the length of the delay"}, {"element": "any delay", "verdict": "contradicted", "evidence": "Delays caused by strikes are excluded"}], "overall": "distorted"}

Source (letter excerpt): 'Writing in 1812, the general reported that his force had fewer than 4,000 effectives, and asked for supplies to be sent urgently.'

Claim to check: 'In 1812, the general commanded an army of 4,000 men.'

Verdict: distorted in two small but real ways.
- '4,000 men' - the source says 'fewer than 4,000 effectives'. The claim rounds a below-4,000 figure up to exactly 4,000.
- 'effectives' are the soldiers fit for duty; the claim's 'army of 4,000 men' turns a count of effectives into the size of the whole force commanded, which the letter does not state.
Accurate version: 'In 1812 the general reported having fewer than 4,000 effectives.'

Source (paper abstract): 'In mice, the compound extended median lifespan by 9%. No human trials have been conducted.'

Headline to check: 'Scientists find compound that extends lifespan by 9%.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "extends lifespan by 9%", "verdict": "distorted", "evidence": "In mice, the compound extended median lifespan by 9% - the result is in mice; the headline drops the species and implies a general, human-relevant finding"}, {"element": "human relevance", "verdict": "unsupported", "evidence": "No human trials have been conducted"}], "overall": "distorted"}

Source (store sign): 'Returns accepted within 30 days, with a receipt. Sale items are final sale and cannot be returned.'

Claim to check: 'You can return anything you buy here within a month.'

Verdict: contradicted.
- 'anything' - the sign excludes a whole category: 'Sale items are final sale and cannot be returned.'
- The claim also drops the receipt condition: returns are accepted 'within 30 days, with a receipt'. Without a receipt, the source promises nothing.
Accurate version: 'Most items can be returned within 30 days with a receipt; sale items are final.'

Source (climate table): 'Monthly rainfall: March 82 mm, April 64 mm, May 91 mm, June 47 mm.'

Claim to check: 'May was the wettest of these four months, with 91 mm of rain.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "May rainfall was 91 mm", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "May 91 mm"}, {"element": "May was the wettest of the four", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "March 82 mm, April 64 mm, May 91 mm, June 47 mm - 91 mm is the largest figure in the table"}], "overall": "supported"}

Source (review excerpt): 'The camera excels in daylight. In low light, image noise is noticeable, and battery drain during video recording is high.'

Claim to check: 'Reviewers say the camera performs excellently in all conditions.'

Verdict: contradicted.
- Daylight performance is supported: 'The camera excels in daylight'.
- 'All conditions' is not: the review flags a weakness in exactly the other condition it discusses - 'In low light, image noise is noticeable'. It also criticises battery drain during video, which the claim ignores.
Accurate version: 'Reviewers praise the camera's daylight performance but note noise in low light.'

Source (planning notice): 'A building of up to 4 storeys is proposed for the site. Public consultation is open until June 30. No decision has been made.'

Claim to check: 'A four-storey building has been approved for the site, and the consultation has closed.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "building has been approved", "verdict": "contradicted", "evidence": "A building of up to 4 storeys is proposed for the site; No decision has been made"}, {"element": "consultation has closed", "verdict": "contradicted", "evidence": "Public consultation is open until June 30"}], "overall": "contradicted"}

Source (programme report): 'After 12 weeks, the training group improved their 5k times by an average of 42 seconds. Individual improvements ranged from 5 seconds to 90 seconds.'

Claim to check: 'Everyone on the programme got about 42 seconds faster.'

Verdict: distorted. The claim turns an average into a uniform result.
- The 42 seconds is a group average: 'improved their 5k times by an average of 42 seconds'.
- The spread is wide: 'Individual improvements ranged from 5 seconds to 90 seconds.' Someone who improved by 5 seconds did not get 'about 42 seconds faster', and neither did the person who gained 90.
Accurate version: 'Participants improved by 42 seconds on average, with individual gains from 5 to 90 seconds.'

Source (ferry notice): 'Foot passengers must check in at least 30 minutes before departure. Passengers with vehicles must check in at least 60 minutes before departure.'

Claim to check: 'You need to check in half an hour before the ferry leaves.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "check in half an hour before departure", "verdict": "distorted", "evidence": "Foot passengers must check in at least 30 minutes before departure - true for foot passengers only; Passengers with vehicles must check in at least 60 minutes before departure"}], "overall": "distorted"}

Source (excavation note): 'The shard bears a partial inscription, possibly a personal name. The remainder of the text is lost.'

Claim to check: 'The inscription on the shard names the pot's owner.'

Verdict: unsupported, leaning on a hedge the claim removes.
- The source is tentative: the inscription is 'possibly a personal name'. It might not be a name at all.
- Even if it is a name, the source never says whose: nothing connects the name to the pot's owner rather than its maker, a dedicator, or anyone else. 'The remainder of the text is lost', so the context that might have settled it is gone.
Accurate version: 'The shard bears a partial inscription that may be a personal name.'

Source (card offer): 'Balance transfers: 0% APR for the first 12 months. A transfer fee of 3% of the amount transferred applies. After 12 months, the standard rate of 24.9% APR applies.'

Claim to check: 'Transfer your balance and you will pay no interest and no fees for a year.'

Return the verdict as JSON only.

{"checks": [{"element": "no interest for a year", "verdict": "supported", "evidence": "0% APR for the first 12 months"}, {"element": "no fees for a year", "verdict": "contradicted", "evidence": "A transfer fee of 3% of the amount transferred applies"}], "overall": "distorted"}

Source (school report): 'The school's pass rate this year is 88%, up from 85% last year. The national average pass rate is 81%.'

Claim to check: 'The school improved by 3 points on last year and now sits 7 points above the national average.'

Verdict: supported. Both derived figures check out against the source.
- Improvement: 88% this year minus 85% last year = 3 points, matching 'improved by 3 points'.
- Gap to the national average: 88% minus 81% = 7 points, matching '7 points above the national average'.
Nothing is rounded, widened or re-based.
